title: Obol Grants Program exists but is currently paused
summary: Obol's own governance docs describe a milestone-based Grants Program across three tracks (SQUAD Goals contributions, retroactive workshop/meetup funding via proof of attendance, and open research/technical contributions to distributed staking), paid in OBOL tokens at USD-equivalent value, applied for via Questbook. The docs page states directly: "The Obol Grants Program is currently paused." No program file exists yet in the registry for this; proposing one with status reflecting the pause rather than active.

programs/obol-grants-program.yaml.name: Obol Grants Program
programs/obol-grants-program.yaml.summary: Milestone-based funding framework for the Obol Collective across three tracks: contributor work on Obol Collective SQUAD Goals, retroactive funding for community workshops/meetups/onboarding sessions (proof of attendance), and open research/technical contributions advancing distributed staking. Grants are issued in OBOL tokens negotiated at USD-equivalent value; applications went through Questbook with no fixed deadlines while live. Per Obol's own docs, the program is currently paused.

summary: CIFAR runs a dedicated AI Catalyst Grants line with its own page, distinct from the Canada CIFAR AI Chairs program: short-term, flexible funding to catalyze new interdisciplinary machine-learning research collaborations, with awards shown across multiple years (2020 through 2026) including a recent AI-safety-focused Catalyst Grants call. No apply URL or award size was disclosed on the page; applicants are directed to contact CIFAR directly.

title: Renaissance Philanthropy's AI for Math Fund missing from registry/programs
summary: Renaissance Philanthropy runs the AI for Math Fund, supporting AI/ML applied to mathematical research: new ML paradigms for mathematical discovery, tools/infrastructure for mathematicians, automated theorem proving, and open mathematical datasets/benchmarks, with a hard open-access requirement (code, datasets, and preprints must be public). The initial $9M round was expanded by an additional $13M announced March 2026; main grants run $100K-$1M for 12-24 months, alongside $20K-$30K summer fellowships and up to $100K seed grants. Abstract submission for the 2026 round closed March 30, 2026, with funding decisions expected August 2026 — still pending as of this check.

All funded code, datasets, and research outputs must be open-access with preprints in public repositories. Initial $9M round expanded by $13M announced March 2026; main grants of $100K-$1M for 12-24 months, plus $20K-$30K summer fellowships and up to $100K seed grants for early-stage work.

title: Emergent Ventures missing as its own program file (already an org-level aka)
summary: Emergent Ventures is listed as an aka on the Mercatus Center org file but has no program file of its own. It's Mercatus's low-overhead fellowship/grant program for 'zero to one' ideas for social improvement, administered by Tyler Cowen, with dedicated tracks for India, Africa, the Caribbean, and Ukraine, plus a COVID-19 science line via its Fast Grants spin-off. Rolling applications, minimum applicant age 13, apply form confirmed live.

title: Hewlett 50 Arts Commissions appears concluded — org profile still cites it as a current example
summary: The org profile names the Hewlett 50 Arts Commissions as an example of an opportunity the foundation 'occasionally opens.' The program's own page on hewlett.org now carries an archive banner: "This page is archived content. It may refer to grants or grantmaking strategies that are no longer active." No open/closed status, deadline, or current award info is given — consistent with the initiative having concluded (its second round funded 10 Bay Area theater/spoken-word commissions). Suggest updating the org profile to stop citing it as a live example.
